key_insight: A fast, morphology-aware JV model can predict organic solar cell performance and stability across complex multi-phase heterojunctions, linking microstructure directly to device behavior.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid screening and design optimization of organic photovoltaic morphologies to balance efficiency, charge transport, and lifetime without relying on expensive full-scale simulations.
method: Models JV curves for up to five morphology phases: donor/acceptor, amorphous/crystalline, and mixed regions.
Uses morphology-aware descriptors for light absorption, exciton dissociation, non-geminate recombination, and charge-carrier mobility.
Runs at very low computation time while remaining suitable for device-level comparison and optimization.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated against Monte Carlo and 3D drift-diffusion simulations and then applied to P3HT:PCBM and PM6:Y6 to study performance-lifetime tradeoffs.
watch_item: The morphology-performance relationship is not universal and depends on the specific materials system, so model transfer across chemistries needs care.
paper_title: Predicting Organic Solar Cell Performance and Stability from Fast, Morphology-aware Current-Voltage Modeling
